title: TOPSTITCH STYLE PROPERTIES: Apply Topstitch Texture
content: ### Objective Change texture type for Topstitch(es). ※ Note : Texture can only be applied when the type is selected for Texture in the Property Editor. ### Location Property Editor ▶ Texture ▶ Search ### Operation 1. Object Browser ▶ Select a Topstitch to add texture image. → The selected Topstitch is now being highlighted. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Topstitch Property Editor ▶ Texture ▶ Search → The Open File window appears. 3. Select and open desired texture image file. → The selected image is now being applied to the selected Topstitch. ※ Note : Not like fabrics, texture image file cannot be applied by Drag & Drop for Topstitch.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for changing the texture type of Topstitches using the Property Editor in your design software.

title: License Key Update With Dongle
content: ### License Key Update ### Objective Set the dongle key when the Network License users want to update their dongle key info. (Currently only available on Windows PC) ### Operation A C2V file is a file sent from the users to the Marvelous Designer Support Team and a V2C file is the other way around (sent from MD back to user). This method enables the users to update their account info / product type / the number of licenses without changing the HASP dongle key. Preparations →HASP dongle key →Update_License.exe file →C2V file →V2C file ### 1\. Creating a C2V file 1\. Plug the HASP Key (dongle) into your computer. 2\. Download and execute the the RUS executable file located at the bottom of this post. 3\. Create C2V file by clicking on Collect Information as below. ![1_1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438777969561) 4\. Once the C2V file successfully created, a message will be printed as below. ![1__.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438788454297) 5\. Submit your C2V file through [**this page**](https://marvelousdesigner.com/teamconsole/keyupdate/1) (Logging in with your Company ID is required). If you experience any difficulties, please contact us via support@marvelousdesigner.com ### 2\. Updating a License Key using V2C file 1\. Download the V2C file sent from Marvelous Designer Support Team. 2\. Click on the link below to access the ACC Page, then select Update/Attach in Options on the left. [ACC Page Link](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) ![2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438778524825) 3\. Click Choose File to find and select the downloaded V2C file. ![3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438794667161) 4\. Click Apply File. ![4.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438778839449) 5\. If the update is successful, the following message will be printed. ![5.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438778982297) ### 3\. Double checking on updated License Key If the License Key Update process is successfully completed, you will be able to double check by following the steps below. 1\. Open a web browser and access to [http://localhost:1947](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) 2\. Make sure all the information is in this part. 3\. Click Features once you see the key info. ![6.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438789202841) 4\. Make sure the number in the red box has been changed correctly. ![7.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438774056729)
content_description: This webpage provides detailed instructions for Network License users to update their HASP dongle key information on Windows PCs using C2V and V2C files.

title: Fold/Sew Pleats
content: ### ### ### ### Objective Create a variety of pleats, fold and sew them (ver2.3.0). ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pleats ▶ Pleats Fold / Pleats Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ Pleats Fold / Pleats Sewing ### Operation #### Pleats Fold 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pleats ▶ Pleats Fold 2D Toolbar ▶ Pleats Fold 2. Click to establish the initial point for the direction of the pleats, then double-click to establish the end point. → Pleats Fold window appears. 3. Select a desired type of pleats. → Depending on the selected pleats type, the Fold Angles of the Internal Lines are now being highlighted. ※ Note: Yellow: Outside fold line (Fold angle of zero(0) degree), Light-blue: Inside fold line (Fold angle of 360 degree), Not highlighted: No fold line (Fold angle of 180 degree) 4. Check Reverse Direction option as needed. → The direction of pleats being folded are now being reversed. 5. Click OK button to complete. #### Pleats Sewing 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pleats ▶ Pleats Sewing 2D Toolbar ▶ Pleats Sewing 2. Click on the initial point and drag up to the end point of the seamline on the pleats Pattern. 3. On the pleats Pattern, click on the first Sewing Line to begin with, and move the mouse to the end point. → Sewing is now being established for every three(3) segments (the amount of segments needed to create each individual pleat). 4. Click on the end point to complete. → The color of the fluorescent sewing lines are now being changed for respective seam color, indicating that the sewing is being completed.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating and sewing various types of pleats using the 2D Pattern tool.

title: Copy/Paste Tack
content: ### Objective Copy and paste tack. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ Edit Tack 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Tack ### Operation #### Copy/Paste Tack 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ Edit Tack 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Tack → The Garment becomes translucent. 2. Right click on the tack to be copied and pasted. → The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Select Copy → The selected tack is copied. 4. Access the right-click pop-up menu again on the copied tack. 5. Select Paste or Mirror Paste. → Preview of the selected tack follows the mouse cursor in 2D and 3D windows. → Any tack outside of the Pattern does not appear in the 3D window. 6. Click the desired location to paste the tack. #### Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Sewing ▶ Tack ▶ Edit Tack 3D Toolbar ▶ Edit Tack → The Garment becomes translucent. 2. Right click on the tack to be duplicated to Symmetric Pattern. → The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Select Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern. → Selected tack is duplicated to the exact same location on its Symmetric Pattern. ※Note: Selected tacks need to be within the same Pattern in order to be duplicated to their Symmetric Patterns.
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for copying, pasting, and duplicating tacks within sewing patterns using the Edit Tack function in the 3D Toolbar.

title: [Size Editor] Adjust Avatar Size (ver. 10)
content: ### ### ### Objective Create an avatar with your own measurements. As Avatar Editor is powered by thousands of real body scan data, even measurements not assigned by users automatically adjust to the most realistic body shape. ### Location Main Menu ▶Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Avatar Size ### Operation 1. Load an Avatar (.avt). Only the avatars provided in ver. 10 V2 and above can be adjusted. 2. Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu ▶Avatar ▶ Avatar Editor ▶ Avatar Size → Measures appear on the Avatar. The editable measures appear in black, whereas the non-editable measures appear in grey. 3. Refer to below graph and adjust the Avatar as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Select Avatar** | Select the Avatar to be edited. This option only appears when two or more Avatars are in the 3D window. **Total Body** | Shape the overall body type with Avatar's height and chest width. In order to get realistic shapes for body parts without assignable measurements, use the Total Body option to create an overall shape and then insert measurements under the Details option. **Height** | Assign Avatar's height. ※Note: * Use the drop-down menu on the right to select the unit of the Height. The default unit follows the program's unit. * Degree of Accuracy based on Height Measure Standard: HPS Height > Inseam > Total Height **Total Height** | Insert the height measured from the ground to the head. ※Note: It is more accurate to assign height with either HPS Height or Inseam option as individual has different head length. The Total Height option is not recommended as it has the lowest accuracy. **HPS Height** | Insert the height measured from the ground to the neck. **Inseam** | Insert the height measured from the ground to the crotch. **Width** | Select and insert desired value as the standard of the overall body width **Details** | Configure Avatar's detailed measurements. Due to a technical reason, a small error may be generated even after inserting a specific measure. The error appears in parentheses next to each measurement and the real measurement can be checked with the measure appears on the Avatar. Edit the Avatar based on the measure appears on the Avatar as the numbers appear in the Avatar Editor only shows the measurements assigned by users. ※Note: * Use the drop-down menu on the right to select the unit of the Height. The default unit follows the program's unit. * Each measurement can be checked with the measure that appears on the Avatar. **Basic** | Use the Basic option when only a small amount of body measurements are available. Unassigned body parts are automatically adjusted based on the real body scan data and the measurements inserted by the user. **Advanced** | Use the Advanced option when available body measurements are abundant. When all measurements under the Advanced options are not available, please use the Basic option to create more realistic body as unassigned measurements are fixed with the default values pre-assigned to each option. **Show All Measurements/** **Show Editable Measurements** | By default, only editable measurements appear in the window. To view all measurements, click the Show All Measurements icon. * Use the Save button to save the adjusted measurements and use the Open button to reload. However, any measurements created with lower versions are not compatible.
content_description: Create and customize your own realistic avatar by adjusting detailed measurements using advanced body scan data for the most accurate representation.

title: Graphics Card Problems and Troubleshooting
content: 1\. By updating the graphics card driver, you can solve and prevent graphics card-related problems that may occur while using the Marvelous Designer software. 2\. Guides you on how to properly connect your desktop graphics card and monitor. ### Applicable for: All users of Marvelous Designer software * * * # **Common Problems** 1\. OpenGL version warning appears when running Marvelous Designer software as shown in the figure below. ![Screen_Shot_2022-10-20_at_9.37.19_PM.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438272879385) 2\. Graphics/texture errors or rendering images appear strange while running Marvelous Designer software. 3\. If the Marvelous Designer GPU-simulation or GPU-rendering speed is lower than the expected performance of your computer's specifications. * * * ## How to Update Graphics Card Driver Step 1) Find out the product name of the graphics card (GPU) installed in your desktop computer or laptop. * As shown in the figure below, you can find the model name of your graphics card (GPU) in the Performance tab of Windows Device Manager. ![002_Task_Manager.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438289814041) Step 2) Search and download the latest driver matching the product name from each manufacturer's website. * Note that even if the graphics card model name looks the same or similar, the drivers for laptops and desktops, and for workstations and servers are different. Search for and install the driver for the type of computer you are using. * [AMD Radeon Driver Download (Link)](https://www.amd.com/en/support) * [Nvidia Driver Download (Link)](https://www.nvidia.com/Download/index.aspx?lang=en) * [Intel Graphics Driver Download (Link)](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/download-center/home.html) Step 3) Run the downloaded driver file. It is recommended to install with administrator privileges. * A computer reboot may be required after driver installation. Follow the on-screen instructions. ![003_RunAsAdministrator.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438273265561) * * * ## Connecting the monitor and graphics card correctly As shown in the figure below, if the monitor cable is connected to the CPU built-in GPU, the built-in GPU is mainly used instead of the external graphics card. OpenGL version warnings may occur when running Marvelous Designer in this situation. ![004_Connectors.JPG](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438293924505) **How to fix** Step 1) Save the files you are working on and turn off the computer completely. Step 2) Connect the monitor cable to the external graphics card and turn on the computer. Connect all monitor cables to the external graphics card, even when using more than one monitor. Step 3) If there is no screen output on the monitor, try reconnecting the monitor power. **See also** * Supported monitor cable types vary depending on the graphic card and monitor. * If you are using the latest monitor and the latest graphic card, most support HDMI or DP (DisplayPort). * Find the right cable for your monitor and graphics card. [Saved search (Link)](https://www.google.com/search?q=monitor+cable+types&oq=monitor+cable) * * * ## Read more * Marvelous Designer software automatically detects the graphics card and driver installed in the computer when launching, and displays a warning if an unsupported graphics card or outdated driver is found. Please refer to the guide above to solve the problem. * If you are using a laptop with an Nvidia graphics card, the laptop will have either an AMD processor or an Intel processor with integrated graphics GPU and Nvidia GPU, respectively, depending on the situation. If an openGL-related error appears while using the Marvelous Designer software, select 'High-performance Nvidia processor' in the Nvidia control panel as shown below and click Apply. ![005_Nvidia_Control_Panel.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438278923929) * If you set Windows Update to 'Auto', it will automatically install the latest graphics card driver. However, the driver provided by the graphics card manufacturer's website is more up-to-date than the Windows update version. * It is recommended to update the graphics card driver at least once every 6 months. It helps with Marvelous Designer software as well as all other graphics programs and overall system performance and stability. * To check GPU usage in Windows, select GPU in the Performance tab of Task Manager as shown below. For Windows 11 users, use a dedicated utility like [GPU-z (freeware, download link)](https://www.techpowerup.com/gpuz/) ![006_CUDA.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438294373401) * If you are using a Mac, the graphics card driver is included in macOS. If you update to the latest macOS, the latest graphics card driver is also installed. * To check CPU-GPU usage on Mac, use the Activity Monitor app built-in to macOS. * Also check the [Marvelous Designer system requirements ](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358219834649)for graphics card-related information.
content_description: This web page provides essential guidance on updating your graphics card driver and properly connecting your monitor to enhance the performance of Marvelous Designer software and resolve related issues.

title: Group Internal Lines and Shapes
content: #### **New in 2025.1** Group with Transform Pattern Group with Edit Pattern Select or Edit Grouped Items with Transform Pattern Ungroup with Transform Pattern #### Group the selected internal lines and pattern shapes. #### ### **Group with Transform Pattern** 1. Select 2 or more internal lines or shapes. Right-click on them to show the context menu. 2. Select **Group** **▶ Group** to group the selected items. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48977895497881)** • A shortcut key for grouping is available. **Function** | **Shortcut** ---|--- **Group** | Windows: Ctrl + G / Mac: Command + G **Ungroup** | Windows: Ctrl + Delete / Mac: Command + Delete; or Command + Fn + Backspace • When grouping or ungrouping internal lines or shapes on one side of a symmetric or half-symmetric pattern, both sides are impacted. • Group relationship is maintained for pattern copy & paste, symmetrical copy, cutting, and merging cases. #### ### ### **Group with Edit Pattern** 1. Select the whole group of internal lines and segment points. Right-click on them to show the context menu. 2. Select **Group** **▶ Group** to group the selected items. **📝Note:** When selecting an incompleted line or point of Internal Line or Shape, the Group menu will not show. #### ### ### **Select or Edit Grouped Items** **with Transform Pattern** 1. Click on the grouped internal lines or shapes to select the whole group. 2. Click again on the individual internal lines or shapes to select individual lines or shapes. #### ### ### **Ungroup with Transform Pattern** 1. Select the grouped internal lines or shapes. Right-click on them to show the context menu. 2. Select **Group** **▶ Ungroup** to remove the group relationship of the selected items.
content_description: Discover the new features in version 2025.1 that enhance your ability to group, edit, and ungroup internal lines and pattern shapes efficiently.

title: Change Pose by Collada's Joint Information
content: ### Objective ※ Note: Only available for file formats with avatar joint information. In this case, COLLADA is being used. As the avatar's joints move when the pose changes, it is possible to change the avatar's pose while keeping the simulation stable even if there is a large difference between the starting and ending poses. However, if the avatar is exported via DAZ Studio, some composition form information may be lost during the process. Therefore, it is necessary to load the posed avatar's OBJ file and adjust the garments after changing the pose. (The avatar's OBJ file only saves the composition form information, so there is no danger of losing information during the loading process.) ### Operation 1. Export a T-pose avatar which can be easily draped and an avatar with the final pose in COLLADA files. To find out export methods from DAZ Studio and Poser in details, check 3D File (COLLADA) Import for the reference. 2. After exporting the COLLADA files, export the avatar poses in OBJ files. 3. Load a posed COLLADA file from the previously saved avatars in program. 4. Click File ▶ Save ▶ Pose to save current avatar as POS file. After dressing T-pose avatar, this file is going to be used when changing current pose. 5. Click File ▶ Open ▶ Avatar to open the previously saved T-pose COLLADA file. Dress the avatar with desired garments. 6. Now Click File ▶ Open ▶ Pose to open the previously saved POS file. The avatar slowly changes poses. It may take a while depending on the complexity of the garments. 7. After the pose changes, load an OBJ file without any loss and adjust garments. Click File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ to open the previously saved final pose OBJ file. Highly positive to observe garments being under the avatar's surface. 8. While simulation is being activated, drag out the parts of the garment that are located under the surface of the avatar by using the left mouse button. To find more details in Select/Move tool, check Move Garment for the reference.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for effectively changing an avatar's pose in COLLADA format while ensuring garment adjustments are made seamlessly and without data loss.

title: Avatar - Smooth and Division (ver.4.2.0)
content: ### Objective Subdivide an Avatar's surface by adjusting its mesh count. The software speed may be reduced when the Avatar mesh count is higher than ideal, please use this feature only when necessary. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Select Avatar ▶ Property Editor ▶ Smooth Avatar ### Operation 1. title: GoZ for Mac
content: ## *** This feature is not currently supported. It will be fixed soon.** GoZ allows direct import/ export of Object between ZBrush and Marvelous Designer. Need to install GoZ installer for GoZ Marvelous Designer Plug-in in ZBrush. ### GoZ Install for Mac Download GoZ installer and Unzip to GoZApps folder To Activate GoZ function, need to installer GoZ Marvelous Designer Plug-in installer from ZBrush. **[Download Installer](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1k1noaAwmFy4I-IbKy7QlhEBXem_RfKxX/view?usp=sharing)** Download installer above, move the installer to GoZApps and unzip. Default Path: /Users/Shared/Pixologic/GoZApps Folder Named MarvelousDesigner will be unzipped. To install GoZ Marvelous Designer, ZBrush need to be installed first. **Install GoZ Marvelous Designer from ZBrush** After unzip Marvelous Designer folder to GoZApps folder, run ZBrush. ZBrush Main menu > Preferences > GoZ > click Force reinstall. List will be displayed, Click Marvelous Designer from the list. Click 'Install' Button to start install. Once installation is completed, Marvelous Designer will be launched, can find GoZ menu on the Marvelous Designer main menu. **Setting Marvelous Designer Path in ZBrush** ZBrush Main menu > Preferences > GoZ > Click Update all paths Browse for desired path of Marvelous Designer and select. ### Run GoZ from Marvelous Designer After installing GoZ Marvelous Designer, can directly export Garment, Avatar and Trims from Marvelous Designer by Run GoZ menu. **Location** Marvelous Designer → Main Menu → GoZ → Run GoZ **Operation** 1. Create or load Garment either Avatar to export by GoZ 2. Select the tool according to the Location above. 3. Garment/ Avatar will be added to ZBrush's Subtool according to GoZ export setting. 4. Once the object is exported by GoZ, can edit and update by Run GoZ button. ### Run GoZ from ZBrush After installing GoZ, can directly export object to Marvelous Designer from ZBrush. **Location** ZBrush → GoZ **Operation** 1. Create an Object from ZBrush. 2. Select the tool according to the Location above. 3. Garment/ Avatar will be exported to Marvelous Designer according to Marvelous Designer's 4. GoZ import setting. 5. Once the object is exported by GoZ, can edit and update by GoZ button. ### GoZ Export Settings GoZ Export setting from Marvelous Designer to ZBrush. **Location** Marvelous Designer → Main Menu → GoZ → Export Settings **Operation** Object | Single Object Exports the selected object as a single object. | Multiple Objects Exports the selected object as multiple objects. ---|---|--- UnWeld Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. | Weld Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. Weld Selected Pattern: Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns. Thin Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. | Thick Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. Include Avatar Shape: Save the Avatar as part of the file. Scale | Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered. *Reset: Reset all GoZ settings to Default. ### GoZ Import Settings GoZ Import setting from ZBrush to Marvelous Designer. **Location** Marvelous Designer → Main Menu → GoZ → Import Settings **Operation** Object Type | Load as Avatar | Imports the object as an avatar and replaces the original avatar with the imported one. ---|---|--- Load as Trim | OBJs that are loaded as Trim do not have collision detection with the 3D Garment and will pass through the 3D Garment when simulated. Load as Garment | Import an Object as Simulation ready Garment, can adjust Physical property from property editor Scale | Manually enter the value. * Reset: Reset all GoZ settings to Default.
content_description: This webpage provides detailed installation and usage instructions for the GoZ Marvelous Designer plug-in, enabling seamless import and export of objects between ZBrush and Marvelous Designer, while noting that the feature is currently unsupported and will be fixed soon.

title: Clone as Pattern/Internal Shape
content: ### Objective Duplicate an Internal Shape as an identical shaped Pattern or vice-versa. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern (A)/ Edit Pattern (Z) 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern ### Operation #### Clone as Pattern (ver2.4.0) 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern (A)/ Edit Pattern (Z) 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2. Right click on the Internal Shape to be duplicated as a Pattern to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Clone as Pattern. →The duplicated Pattern follows along the mouse cursor. 3. Click on the 2D window to place the Pattern. #### Clone as Pattern (With Sewing) (ver. 12.2) 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern (A) / Edit Pattern (Z) 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2. Right click on the Internal Shape to be duplicated as a Pattern to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Clone as Pattern (With Sewing). →The duplicated Pattern follows along the mouse cursor. →Sewing lines are automatically generated between the selected Internal Shape and the duplicated Pattern, except in the following cases; * Where a Segment does not have angle between its first and last points. (Where two points are on a straight line) * Where the selected segments are not connected to each other. 3. Click on the 2D window to place the pattern. #### Clone as Internal Shape 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Pattern (A)/ Edit Pattern (Z) 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern 2. Right click on the Pattern to be duplicated as an Internal Shape to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Clone as Internal Shape. →The duplicated Internal Shape follows along the mouse cursor. 3. Click on the desired Pattern to place the Internal Shape. ※ Note: Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard while pasting the duplicated Pattern/Internal Shape to move it on a straight line or on a diagonal line.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for duplicating internal shapes into identical patterns and vice versa within a 2D design interface.

title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Stretch-Weft/Warp, Shear
content: ### Objective Use the Weft, Warp and Shear intensities to show the resistance against the horizontal, vertical and diagonal elasticity according to the 2D window. Increasing the Shear intensity to the same ratio as the Weft and Warp intensities, is going to express materials that creases easily such as cotton and denim. On the other hand, decreasing the intensity value is going to express more elastic materials such as silk and jersey. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ Stretch-Weft/Warp, Shear ![sheeer.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438828954265)
content_description: Explore how Weft, Warp, and Shear intensities influence fabric elasticity and resistance in the Fabric Property Editor, allowing for precise manipulation of material characteristics like creasing and stretch.

title: CREATE CUSTOM BUTTON TEXTURE: Create Button Texture
content: ### Objective Create and apply custom textures to buttons in CLO in order to express various button styles. ※ Note: Adobe Photoshop is needed to create custom button texture. ### Operation 1. Download custom button texture templates (.psd) provided in the Library window: ※ Note: Choose your desired button design and download respective custom button texture file as needed. ![33.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438838867353) 2. Open downloaded .psd file in Adobe Photoshop. → The template is divided into three parts each representing front, back, and thread of the button. 3. Open a texture image to be embedded to the template. → The texture will open in a new tab in Adobe Photoshop. 4. Follow the path: Main Menu → Edit → Define Pattern → The selected texture will be added as a pattern in Adobe Photoshop. 5. In the Layer Window, select the desired layer to be painted with the defined pattern. The Layer Window is located along the right side of the Adobe Photoshop Window. 6. While the desired layer is selected, left click on the Paint tool and select the defined pattern → The selected layer will be painted with the chosen pattern. 7. Hide UV and Test layers, then save the image. ※ Note: Saving the image in .jpeg format is recommended.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating and applying custom textures to buttons in CLO, using Adobe Photoshop to enhance button styles.

title: Create Pin
content: ### Objective Affix specific portions of the Garment and utilize Pin similar to the Freeze function. It is also convenient when turning/flipping over collars, lapels, or cuffs. ### Location #### Pin Tool Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Pin (Box) / Pin (Lasso) 3D Toolbar ▶ (Click for more than 2 seconds) ▶ Pin (Box) / Pin (Lasso) #### Select/Move Tool Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Select/Move 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ### Operation #### Pin Tool 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Pin (Box) / Pin (Lasso) 3D Toolbar ▶ (Click more than 2 seconds) ▶ Pin (Box) / Pin (Lasso) → The Garment mesh is now displayed in red in both the 3D and 2D windows. 2. Click on a vertex (a point of the mesh). → A Pin is created on the selected point. 3. Or click on a desired area on the Garment ▶ Click and drag to select the area. → Pins are created on the vertex of the selected area. → Pins can also be created on 2D Patterns. 4. Click and drag, or use the Gizmo to move the pinned mesh as desired in the 3D window. ※ Note: Click and drag on the 2D Pattern while pressing Shift+Ctrl on the keyboard to create additional pinned areas. Adversely, click and drag on the 2D Pattern while pressing Ctrl on the keyboard to remove Pins from existing pinned areas. #### Select/Move Tool 1. Click on the Select/Move tool in the 3D window. 2. Click while pressing W on the keyboard to create a Pin on a specific point. → A Pin is created on the selected point. 3. If the input language is set to Korean, a Pin cannot be created when pressing W on the keyboard. Make sure to change the input language to English. ※ Note: * #### Create Pin on Segment Double-click on a Pattern outline in either the 3D or 2D window to create Pins on a segment. When creating Pins on the Pattern in the 2D window, Pins are generated on adjacent segment vertices when the angle difference is less than 20˚. * #### Create Pin on Pattern Double-click on a Pattern in either the 3D or 2D window to create Pins on a Pattern. * #### Create Pin on Internal Line (ver4.0.0) Use the same procedure as above to create Pins on specific Internal Lines and Shapes.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on using the Pin Tool for affixing garment portions and manipulating collar, lapel, and cuff designs in a 3D garment editing environment.

title: Initial setup/options when first-launching the software
content: ### Objective Version -Enterprise Network (Online Authentication) -Academic Perpetual (Online Authentication) ### Operation 1. Double-click on the icon on the Desktop to launch the program. 2. The login pop-up window appears as below. 3. Enter ID and password. 4. Adjust the options as needed and select Log In. Left click on the drop-down arrow to access further options. Save ID | Save the entered ID in the registry. ---|--- Save PW | Save the entered password in the registry. If using 'Firewall', Please check this option in the login window | Login through the client server. Use Proxy Server (This option not available from MD11 on) | When user uses the proxy server, the proxy server information is needed to be properly certified. To use the proxy server, toggle on the check box and enter corresponding proxy information. ※Note: To use proxy server, please toggle on Use Proxy Server and enter proxy information. 5. Adjust below options as needed. Units | Set default unit. ---|--- Language | Set default language View Control | Choose View Control presets optimized for respective mouse and program type. To adjust the setting individually, navigate to Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ View Control. Graphic Options | Antialiasing | Adjust the setting to smooth out the outline of the object. As the value increases, smoother the outline is and slower the rendering speed is. Show Shadow | Show or hide shadow in the 3D Window. Use VBOs | Set VBOs usage to improve the rendering speed. Use Normal Maps | Use or unuse Normal Maps which express seamlines and textures more realistically. 6. Select OK to run the program.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for logging into the Enterprise Network and Academic Perpetual online authentication systems, including options for user settings and graphic adjustments.

title: Apply Button Style
content: ### Objective Apply button styles onto buttons as desired. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ### Operation #### Apply Button Style In Property Editor 1. Click on a button and select a button style in the Property Editor. → The selected button style is now being applied to the button. #### Select A Button And Apply Button Style 1. Select a button. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Assigned to Selected Patterns → The button style is now being applied to the selected button. #### Select A Button And Apply A New Button Style 1. Select a button. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Assigned to New Fabric → A new buttonhole style is now being added to the buttonhole list window and applied at the same time.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for applying and customizing button styles using the Property Editor in the Object Browser.

title: Optimize Curve Points
content: ## Objective Optimize the number of curve points on Patterns and Internal Lines to ease the Pattern editing process (ver3.0.0). ### ## Optimize All Curve Points ### Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ Optimize All Curve Points ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline in the Location above. 2. Optimize Curve Points dialog appears, and the number of curve points is automatically applied as an optimized ratio. (ver.7.3.0) Curve Points | Adjust the ratio of curve points by a percentage (%). ※ The closer to 0% it is, the fewer curve points there will be. But there may be deviations from the original curvature. ---|--- Reset | Reset the applied ratio of curve points while the dialog is running. Apply | Apply the Optimize Curve Points based on the input ratio. Close | Close the Optimize Curve Points dialog. ## Optimize Curve Points ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Transform Pattern(A), Edit Pattern(Z) 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern(A), Edit Pattern(Z) ### ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline in the Location above. 2. Right-click your mouse on the desired patterns or segments, and select Optimize Curve Points. 3. Optimize Curve Points dialog appears, and the number of curve points is automatically applied as an optimized ratio. (ver.7.3.0) Curve Points | Adjust the ratio of curve points by a percentage (%). ※ The closer to 0% it is, the fewer curve points there will be. But there may be deviations from the original curvature. ---|--- Reset | Reset the applied ratio of curve points while the dialog is running. Apply | Apply the Optimize Curve Points based on the input ratio. Close | Close the Optimize Curve Points dialog.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on optimizing curve points in Patterns and Internal Lines to streamline the pattern editing process.

title: Move Fastened Button/Buttonhole
content: ### Objective Move a fastened button only, or a button and buttonhole together. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ### Operation #### Move Fastened Button Only 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button 2. Click and drag the desired button in the 2D or 3D window. → The selected button is moved to where the mouse is released. → The moved button stays fastened. #### Move Fastened Button and Buttonhole 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button 2. Hold down Shift on the keyboard, then click all buttons and buttonholes to be moved in the 2D or 3D window. 3. Click and drag the selected buttons and buttonholes. → The selected buttons and buttonholes are moved to where the mouse is released. → The moved buttons and buttonholes stay fastened.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for moving a fastened button or both a button and its corresponding buttonhole within a 2D or 3D design interface.

title: Convert to Hole/Internal Shape
content: ### Objective Create a hole based on an Internal Shape or fill in a hole by converting it to an Internal Shape. ### Location #### Convert to Hole Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Internal Shape) ▶ Convert to Hole #### Convert to Internal Shape Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Hole) ▶ Convert to Internal Shape ### Operation #### Convert to Hole 1. Select Transform Pattern tool or Edit Pattern tool. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Internal Shape) ▶ Convert to Hole →The selected Internal Shape is converted to hole. (If you are using versions lower than ver2.3.0, Select Sync Tool.) #### Convert to Internal Shape 1. Select Transform Pattern tool or Edit Pattern tool. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Hole) ▶ Convert to Internal Shape →The selected hole is converted to Internal Shape. (If you are using versions lower than ver2.3.0, Select Sync tool.)
content_description: This webpage provides step-by-step instructions for converting internal shapes to holes and vice versa using the Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern tools.

title: Polygon
content: ### Objective Create polygon Patterns in 2D Window. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Polygon 2D Toolbar ▶ Polygon ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ Polygon 2D Toolbar ▶ Polygon 2. Click on the 2D window to make the start point. 3. Drag the mouse and click as needed to freehand a polygon. 4. Right click while freehanding a polygon. → The Create Polygon window appears. 5. Length or Mirror Creation options to create polygon more precisely and conveniently. Option | Description ---|--- Length | Length | Designate the length to be created next. When the Mirror Creation option is active, the Length will be applied to the mirrored line as well. Option (ver5.1.0) | Mirror Creation | The polygon is created symmetrically. The starting point converts to a closed point. Axis | Local | Symmetric lines are created based on the starting point (local). X-Axis | Symmetric lines are created based on the X-Axis. Y-Axis | Symmetric lines are created based on the Y-Axis. 6. Click again on the start point to complete the polygon. ※ Note: * Pressing the keyboard’s Delete key while setting points to create a pattern cancels the points, starting from the most recent one. Furthermore, pressing the Esc/Ctrl+Z key during creation cancels the entire operation. * While making points to create a Pattern, holding down the Ctrl key and setting points turns segment points into Free Curve Points. This creates a polygon Pattern made up of curved lines. * Setting a Segment Point while holding down shift reveals a guideline that can move horizontally, vertically, and diagonally at a 45 degree angle according to the Segment Point. ※ Note: Create Pattern Tool Group ※ Note: Mirror Creating
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for users to effortlessly create custom polygon patterns in a 2D window using various tools and options for precision.

title: Usage - Trims and Details
content: You can use various default items within Marvelous Designer. Also, you can import different types of OBJ or FBX files you made into the software to use them. ### Manual - Trims and Details * Topstitch: [https://marvelousdesigner.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/sections/47114832113561](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/sections/47114832113561) * Button: [https://marvelousdesigner.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/sections/36123975345561](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/sections/36123975345561) * To find more, please follow the link below and refer to the 'Express Details' [https://marvelousdesigner.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/sections/360007305872](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/sections/360007305872) ### How to put the OBJ trims on an avatar using the Morph Target You can put various OBJ trims which is very tight on your avatar using the Morph Target * Follow the path below to load a file * File -> Import/Import (Add) -> OBJ -> OBJ Dialog Window * Load Type: Add * Object Type: Avatar * Automatically Add Arrangement Points: Unchecked * Auto Create Fitting Suit: Unchecked * You can increase or decrease the size of a trim imported to the software by clicking the scale icon from the gizmo. It is recommended that you do not change the placement of the trim. It could interrupt the stable simulation if the position of the trim changes after being imported. * Simulate the garment to fit into the trim * Once the simulation completed, import the original trim file as Morph Target * File -> Import/Import (Add) -> OBJ -> OBJ Dialog Window * Load Type: Add * Object Type: Morph TargetM * Morphing Frame Count: 30 (Input the desired number of frames.)
content_description: Discover how to enhance your designs in Marvelous Designer by using default items and importing OBJ or FBX files, along with detailed instructions for applying trims and details to your avatars.

title: Can I import my own avatar?
content: Marvelous Designer does support different types of 3D file formats for our users. You can import your own avatar to Marvelous Designer so that you create various fabric items for/with it. **Manual - 3D File Import / Export** Manual Link ([OBJ](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358223288601)/[FBX](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358232885017-3D-File-FBX-Import-Export)/[Alembic](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358253053081-3D-File-Alembic-Import-Export)/[OpenCOLLADA](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358302910361-3D-File-COLLADA-Import)) * **Import an avatar without joints** * The file types Marvelous Designer supports are as below. In general, most avatar files that do not contain animation cache in it can be imported as the suggested formats. * OBJ, FBX, Alembic, OpenCOLLADA * **Import an avatar with joints** * An avatar with animation cache is recommended to be imported to Marvelous Designer as suggested file types below. * FBX, Alembic
content_description: Explore how to import and export various 3D file formats in Marvelous Designer to create custom fabric items with your own avatars.
